thread:
lina: quick check — I think the rerank API docs have the 'scores' example reversed compared to the actual response shape. saw it when validating a customer sample.

lina: example in docs shows [0.9, 0.1] mapped to items [A, B], but the actual API returns scores in the same index order as candidates (so B would be 0.1). can we confirm?

tom: good catch. which file / line?

lina: docs/reference/rerank.md — the response example under 'Response schema' block. i pasted the snippet here:

```json
{
  "candidates": ["A", "B"],
  "scores": [0.9, 0.1]
}
```

lina: that makes it look like the top score corresponds to A always. but our service returns candidates in original order and scores align by index. so code samples that zip(candidates, scores) are fine, but the prose implying sorted-by-score is wrong.

raj: hmm yup. internal model returns same order, we only provide a separate "ranked" field when we reorder. not many calls use that though.

kate: customer reported they assumed scores were sorted and built a UI that highlighted the wrong item. we should push a patch ASAP.

tom: i'll take the docs PR. i'll update the example to show both: raw response + a snippet that demonstrates how to produce a ranked list by sorting indices.

tom: proposed snippet:

```python
# raw response
candidates = ["A", "B"]
scores = [0.9, 0.1]
# to get ranked indices
ranked = sorted(range(len(scores)), key=lambda i: scores[i], reverse=True)
ranked_items = [candidates[i] for i in ranked]
```

lina: perfect. also update the prose to explicitly say "scores align with candidates by index; use the ranked example to sort by score."

tom: adding tests and a small note to the migration guide (we changed this in the v2 API docs earlier but missed this endpoint). linking PR in a sec.

lina: preview looks good, thanks. one more thing — the Go SDK example currently assumes scores are floats but the generated SDK returns []float32 not []float64, which caused a json.Unmarshal mismatch in our docs snippet. can we make the Go snippet use the SDK type?

raj: SDK change happened in sdk-gen last month; types are float32 everywhere to save bytes. docs should show the SDK usage, not raw json types. tom can we include `[]float32` example?

tom: yep will update Go example to use sdk.Score (alias float32) and include a short note: "SDK types may differ from raw JSON types (float32 vs float64). use the SDK model objects when possible."

kate: can you also add a migration blurb for customers upgrading from v1 -> v2 about score ordering expectations? simple bullet under breaking changes.

lina: agreed. small bullet with example code in py and go to avoid more confusion.

tom: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/4238 — includes updated rerank.md, migration note, and Go/Python snippets.

lina: awesome. i'll do a quick review and approve. thanks everyone :tada:
